# Validate Platform Operator platform status and FIPS remediation scope

## Description

The strategy lists Platform Operator as an affected component of the FIPS 140-3
compliance effort, but no architecture context file exists for it in the
platform inventory, so its platform status, owning repos, shipped images, build
pipeline, and cryptographic posture cannot be substantiated. This investigation
resolves those unknowns and produces the findings needed to scope the Platform
Operator crypto remediation work.

## Scope

- Confirm Platform Operator's status in the platform: owning repositories
  (upstream/midstream), the set of shipped images, and build pipeline status
- Audit each shipped image for non-validated cryptographic library usage:
  inventory linked crypto libraries, classify each as validated or
  non-validated, and note request-path exposure
- Determine the remediation approach per affected image (validated crypto
  alternatives, base image strategy, rebuild requirements)
- Deliverable: a findings report with the per-image crypto inventory and a
  remediation recommendation sufficient to scope the remediation work

## Acceptance Criteria

- Platform Operator's platform status is confirmed and documented: owning
  repositories, shipped image set, and build pipeline status
- Every shipped Platform Operator image is inventoried with its linked crypto
  libraries classified as validated or non-validated, with request-path
  exposure noted
- A remediation recommendation exists for each affected image
- Findings are handed off to the remediation team

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): enables — the findings determine whether and how the Platform
  Operator images can meet the validated-crypto requirement

# FIPS crypto remediation for KServe control-plane and data-plane images

## Description

Replace non-validated cryptographic library usage in KServe-owned serving-stack
images so the model serving stack runs correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift
clusters using validated crypto modules, with no non-validated crypto in the
request path.

## Scope

- Identify non-validated crypto usage across KServe control-plane and
  data-plane images: the controller, inference service data-plane containers
  (predictor, transformer, explainer), queue proxy, storage initializer, and
  router
- Remediate each affected image: switch to validated crypto modules and
  FIPS-compatible builds/base images
- Rebuild the remediated images and validate the serving stack on a FIPS-enabled
  OpenShift cluster (serverless and raw deployment modes where applicable)
- Confirm no functional regression on non-FIPS clusters

## Acceptance Criteria

- No KServe-owned serving-stack image contains non-validated crypto in the
  request path, verified by binary/library inspection of each image
- InferenceService resources deploy and serve inference requests correctly on a
  FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster (Ready status conditions reached; sample
  inference requests succeed)
- No functional regression on non-FIPS clusters
- Rollback: the pre-remediation image builds remain available and deployable,
  so a cluster affected by a regression can revert to the previous image
  versions
- Build pipeline is green for all remediated images

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): all serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters
  using validated crypto modules

# FIPS compliance evidence package and certification submission

## Description

Assemble the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the remediated model
serving stack — module inventory, build attestations, and test results — and
submit it through the security review board to the external accredited
certification lab. The package spans two components: KServe evidence is
produced within RHOAI Serving, while the Platform Operator evidence (image
inventory, build attestations, and test results) is contributed by the
Platform Operator team's remediation work. This epic, owned by RHOAI Serving,
coordinates those contributions and owns the single assembled package and its
submission — one logical deliverable across contributing teams.

## Scope

- Produce the module inventory: validated crypto modules per serving-stack
  image
- Collect build attestations for all remediated images
- Collect FIPS-mode test results from the cluster validation of the remediated
  serving stack
- Assemble the package in the format required by the security review board and
  the certification lab
- Shepherd the package through security review board sign-off milestones and
  submit it to the external lab

## Acceptance Criteria

- Module inventory covers every serving-stack image in scope
- Build attestations exist for all remediated images
- FIPS-mode test results are included
- The package passes security review board sign-off at the defined milestones
- The package is submitted to the external certification lab
- Lab scheduling and review-board cadence are externally controlled and cannot
  be compressed by engineering effort; submission timing is a schedule risk,
  not a work-scope item

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): compliance evidence package (module inventory, build
  attestations, test results) assembled and submitted through the security
  review board to the external certification lab
